title: Debugging MCP Like an Operator
objective: After this lesson you will be able to drive the MCP Inspector across tools/resources/prompts, trace requests through JSON-RPC with correlation IDs, negotiate versions explicitly, and read error codes to fixes.
why: 'The agent can't see my tool' is the #1 MCP support question, and answers live in exactly four places: discovery (advertised?), transport (framing intact?), validation (args rejected?), versions (mutual?). Operators check in that order with tools that show each layer. Debugging MCP is layered elimination, not log-diving.

blocks.text: The **MCP Inspector** connects to any server for interactive verification: **tools/list** (advertised? names/descriptions/schemas as intended?), **tools/call** with forms (valid args pass, invalid reject pre-handler?), **resources/read** (URIs resolve?), **prompts/get** (templates render?). Run all four on every change — most 'agent' bugs reproduce here as server bugs in seconds.

Debug in stack order, never randomly: (1) **transport** — framing intact? (stdout clean? connection alive?); (2) **discovery** — server/discover returns expected versions + capabilities?; (3) **validation** — args rejected? (read the isError text — it names the rule); (4) **versions** — mutual spec support or explicit error?; (5) **semantics** — handler logic with logged inputs. Each layer exonerated moves exactly one level deeper.

blocks.caption: Elimination order encoded: transport → discovery → validation → versions → semantics

blocks.text: Notifications and versions in the wild

Dynamic tool lists need **subscriptions/listen** for `toolsListChanged` with re-list on event — plus polling fallback (delivery is best-effort). Mixed-version fleets negotiate per server/discover: pin versions, test the matrix (client vX × server vY), and read explicit version errors as routing instructions, not failures.

blocks.title: Eliminate by layers
blocks.note: Run it: expect transport, discovery, validation, then all-green — first failing layer owns the incident. Elimination order prevents log-diving: check transport before reading a single handler line.

items: Inspector across list/call/read/get on every change — most agent bugs reproduce as server bugs
Eliminate transport → discovery → validation → versions → semantics; first failure owns it
Notifications opt-in with polling fallback; versions negotiated explicitly per fleet matrix

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice diagnoser on all four contexts and map layers. (b) Write the incident report for 'refund tool vanished mid-conversation': three candidate layers with the check that rules each in/out. (c) State the polling fallback rule for toolsListChanged and why best-effort demands it.
hints: Mappings: transport / discovery / validation / all-green (in order) — first failure owns.
Candidates: notification missed (check subscription + re-list manually) vs server redeploy dropping the tool (discover shows absence) vs permission revoked (scope audit) — each with its ruling check.
Polling fallback: re-list on interval regardless (delivery best-effort across reconnects); notifications optimize, polling guarantees.
exercise.why: Layered incident reports (candidate + ruling check each) plus fallback design (best-effort + guarantee pairing) are operator-grade debugging — practiced on realistic disappearances.
exercise.code: // Incident-report pattern: candidates × ruling-checks, ordered by layer.

quiz.q: 'Agent can't see my new tool.' First check?
options: Inspector tools/list: advertised? (Then transport framing, then versions — layered order, discovery before depth)
quiz.explain: Advertisement precedes invocation: list first, then framing, versions, validation, semantics. Most such bugs die at step one.

quiz.q: toolsListChanged missed across a reconnect. Design implication?
options: Best-effort delivery demands polling fallback: interval re-list guarantees freshness, notifications optimize it
quiz.explain: Best-effort means gaps are normal, especially across reconnects. Polling guarantees; notifications accelerate.

quiz.q: isError result names a violated pattern. Value?
options: Self-diagnosing failures: the violated rule travels with the failure — fix location named, not inferred
quiz.explain: Named violations convert debugging from inference to reading. Schema-driven errors carry their own diagnosis.

summary: Inspector per change, layered elimination per incident, notifications with polling fallback, versions negotiated explicitly. Operators debug layers, not logs.
